title: Pelvic Pain

rationale.Pelvic US with Doppler: Enlarged ovary, decreased/absent flow. Normal Doppler doesn't exclude.

hpi: {{patient_name}} presents with acute onset severe unilateral pelvic pain, nausea, vomiting, and possibly low-grade fever. Pain is sudden, severe, and may have occurred intermittently before (partial torsion). Ovarian torsion is a GYNECOLOGIC EMERGENCY — the ovary twists on its vascular pedicle → venous and lymphatic outflow obstruction → arterial compromise → ovarian ischemia and necrosis if not detorsed within hours. Risk: ovarian mass/cyst, pregnancy, ovulation induction. Diagnosis: pelvic ultrasound with Doppler — enlarged ovary, decreased/absent arterial and venous flow. However, normal Doppler does NOT exclude torsion (may be intermittent or only venous flow absent). Treatment: EMERGENCY surgical exploration with detorsion (preserve ovary if viable) ± oophoropexy. Do NOT delay surgery for imaging if high clinical suspicion.
